trust_decision.summary: An int32 payload length read off the wire in a plaintext (pre-auth) MTProto message must be validated as non-negative and as not exceeding the bytes actually remaining in the buffer before MessageData is allocated; at the pinned commit Decode allocates straight from the wire value and only ConsumeN checks the bound afterwards, so a hostile peer causes either a 2 GB allocation or a makeslice panic.

landing_point.why: The report names proto.UnencryptedMessage.Decode; the unchecked make([]byte, dataLen) is the first thing an engineer looking for that function sees.

fix_sites.entry_point: proto.UnencryptedMessage.Decode, reached from exchange.unencryptedWriter.readUnencrypted (exchange/proto.go:76-83), exchange.ClientExchange.Run (exchange/client_flow.go:151-156) and exchange.ServerExchange.Run (exchange/server_flow.go:107,143,244); public wrappers exchange.Exchanger.Client/Server (exchange/flow.go:106,123) and mtproto.Conn.runExchange (mtproto/connect.go:111-120)
fix_sites.module_kind: library: core protocol decoder, package proto

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The advisory names one decoder in proto/; the abridged transport codec is a different layer and a legacy/rarely used MTProto transport, and its 24-bit length caps the damage at ~64 MB rather than 2 GB, so a solver can reasonably call it unrelated and leave it.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: A message whose declared length exactly equals the bytes remaining must still decode and consume the buffer (that is the normal single-frame case, since Recv delivers one frame and callers then do b.ResetTo(msg.MessageData)); MessageData must also stay a private copy because callers reuse the same Buffer for the next write. An over-broad guard (rejecting dataLen >= b.Len(), rejecting dataLen == 0, or adding an absolute cap) breaks every valid exchange message or aliases caller memory.

O6_input_shapes: negative int32 dataLen (would panic in make) - rejected by fix.diff:22-27
dataLen greater than b.Len() (huge allocation before ConsumeN can reject) - rejected by fix.diff:28-30
in-bounds dataLen, including dataLen == b.Len() and dataLen == 0, unchanged and still accepted (no absolute cap is added)

O8_uncovered_routes.route: Abridged transport frame length: readAbridged reads a 1- or 3-byte length (4 bytes via b.Int, max 0xFFFFFF) and does b.ResetN(n << 2) with no positivity or maxMessageSize check before any payload byte arrives, unlike intermediate/padded/full which go through readLen.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: Another layer from the advisory (transport framing, not the plaintext message decoder) and a legacy codec; the value is only 24 bits so the allocation is capped at ~64 MB, so it can be argued not to be 'the same' unbounded allocation.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: 1 package from the landing point (proto -> proto/codec), plus transport/detect_codec.go and transport/listener.go which let a remote peer select it

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A second length-prefixed message decoder in proto (e.g. an extended message container, or a Message variant for a newer container id) that repeats make([]byte, m.Bytes) and drops the 1 MB guard.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: proto already ships two wire decoders with a length-prefixed body (container Message with a 1 MB cap, UnencryptedMessage without one); a maintainer adding a container variant would copy the neighbour.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A fifth transport codec whose read path is written from readAbridged instead of readLen.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: readAbridged already diverges from the three other codecs, so any new or forked codec inherits the missing bound.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A third plaintext-message call site that decodes the header itself and grows its own length pre-check or its own make(), rather than calling proto.UnencryptedMessage.Decode.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: This file already decodes a plaintext message outside readUnencrypted, so an inline variant is an established pattern in the same package.

O9_family: unbounded/excessive memory allocation from an untrusted wire length (CWE-770, CWE-789)

O10_build.toolchain: go 1.25.0 (go.mod:3), pure-Go module deps resolved from go.sum, no vendor directory
O10_build.project_tests: proto/unencrypted_message_test.go covers only the Encode/Decode roundtrip; exchange/flow_test.go and exchange/fuzz_test.go drive the whole pre-auth exchange over an in-memory transport.Intermediate pipe (exchange/flow_test.go:34-35), so the affected path is testable offline

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Add only the bound the solver reproduced (either int(dataLen) > b.Len() and forget the negative makeslice panic, or the reverse), then validate through Encode/round-trip, and stop at proto/ without looking at the abridged frame length.

out_of_scope_notes: crypto/encrypted_message_data.go:94-100 compares MessageDataLen only against the padding length and leaves the negative check to cipher_decrypt.go:52-59 - post-auth path, noted and not pursued.
proto/codec/abridged.go:139 also accepts a zero-length frame, which readLen rejects for the other codecs - part of the same O8 route, not pursued further.
unverified: repo_mb not measurable without a shell; a glob found 3864 .go files including the generated tg/, mt/ and gen/ trees, so the tree is far above the 5 MB tiny threshold.

Whether the abridged transport codec counts as 'the same protected sink' for O8 is a judgement call: every call site that reaches proto.UnencryptedMessage.Decode (exchange/proto.go:76, exchange/client_flow.go:151) is covered by the single fixed hunk, so there is no uncovered route into the fixed function itself.

O7: no local schema or cache produces the protected length - it is wire-supplied. Recorded as serializer because UnencryptedMessage.Encode is the only local producer and Decode never calls it, so a fix validated through an Encode/Decode roundtrip cannot generate the malicious shape; the producer sits in the same package, hence j_cause_other_layer = 0.
latest tree was not provided, so present_in_latest is unknown; full advisory text was not provided either - screening used the summary and the fix diff only.
